title: fix: resolve async factory services in dispatcher and all framework adapters
body:
`kernel.getService('auth')`, `kernel.getService('analytics')`, and `kernel.context.getService('protocol')` throw `"Service 'X' is async - use await"` when registered via async factory (PluginLoader). The dispatcher's internal `getService()`, direct `protocol` service lookups, and all adapter auth lookups used the sync path, which the kernel rejects for Promise-returning factories.

### Dispatcher (`http-dispatcher.ts`)

- Introduced `resolveService(name)` helper with full fallback chain: `getServiceAsync` → `getService` (sync) → `context.getService` → services Map. Each step checks for non-null results before returning, ensuring proper fallthrough.
- `getService()` delegates to `resolveService()` for all CoreServiceName lookups.
- `getObjectQLService()` simplified to use `resolveService()`.
- Fixed 6 occurrences of `this.kernel.context.getService('protocol')` in `handleMetadata()` and `handleUi()` — these used the same sync path that throws for async factory services.

```typescript
private async resolveService(name: string) {
    if (typeof this.kernel.getServiceAsync === 'function') {
        try {
            const svc = await this.kernel.getServiceAsync(name);
            if (svc != null) return svc;
        } catch { }
    }
    if (typeof this.kernel.getService === 'function') {
        try {
            const svc = await this.kernel.getService(name);
            if (svc != null) return svc;
        } catch { }
    }
    if (this.kernel?.context?.getService) {
        try {
            const svc = await this.kernel.context.getService(name);
            if (svc != null) return svc;
        } catch { }
    }
    return this.getServicesMap()[name];
}
```

### Framework Adapters (all 7)

- Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit, NestJS, Nuxt — auth service resolution switched from sync `getService` to async-first pattern with graceful fallback:

```typescript
let authService: AuthService | null = null;
try {
    if (typeof kernel.getServiceAsync === 'function') {
        authService = await kernel.getServiceAsync<AuthService>('auth');
    } else if (typeof kernel.getService === 'function') {
        authService = kernel.getService<AuthService>('auth');
    }
} catch {
    authService = null;
}
```

### All affected services

- `auth`, `analytics`, `metadata`, `file-storage`, `automation` — via `getService()` → `resolveService()`
- `objectql` — via `getObjectQLService()` → `resolveService()`
- `protocol` — 6 direct `context.getService()` calls replaced with `resolveService('protocol')`

### Tests

- 7 new dispatcher tests for `getServiceAsync` preferred path (analytics, auth, automation, file-storage, protocol, null fallthrough, error fallthrough)
- `getServiceAsync` adapter tests for Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit
- All 244 tests pass (55 dispatcher + 189 adapter)

Fully backward-compatible — falls through to sync path when `getServiceAsync` is unavailable.

> <issue_description># Synchronous getService Error for Async Auth & Analytics Services
> 
> ## Problem Statement
> Calling `getService('analytics')` or `getService('auth')` via the ObjectStack Kernel (ObjectKernel/LiteKernel) throws the following runtime error if the service was registered with an async factory:
> 
> ```
> Error: Service 'analytics' is async - use await
> Error: Service 'auth' is async - use await
> ```
> 
> ## Impacted Components
> - `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts` — Dispatcher uses private `getService()` which calls sync `kernel.getService()`
> - Kernel & Dispatcher call chain (`dispatcher.handleAnalytics`, `dispatcher.handleAuth`)
> - All adapter plugins (Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit, NestJS) that rely on `kernel.getService('auth')` or `kernel.getService('analytics')`
> - Plugins/services registered via async factory (e.g. PluginLoader)
> 
> ## Root Cause
> - `getService()` uses the synchronous path but some services (auth, analytics) were registered as async factories (via dependency injection in PluginLoader).
> - When the service lookup resolves to a Promise, kernel throws to avoid returning a Promise from a sync API.
> - Dispatcher and adapters frequently use sync getService, which breaks if consumers are not migrated to async path.
> 
> ## Code Evidence
> - [`kernel.ts`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/spec/blob/main/packages/core/src/kernel.ts): Throws when service is async but called via sync API.
> - [`http-dispatcher.ts`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/spec/blob/main/packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts): Dispatcher sync service lookup fails for async services.
> - Service interfaces (`IAnalyticsService`, `IAuthService`) are Promise-based, and actual plugin implementations often use async factories for setup.
> - Test files simulate both sync and async scenarios (see `*.test.ts` for dispatcher, adapters).
> 
> ## Solution Proposal
> - **Refactor `http-dispatcher.ts` and all adapters:**
>     - Use an explicit `getServiceAsync()` method for service registry lookup when factory-based services are possible.
>     - Ensure `dispatcher.handleAuth` and `dispatcher.handleAnalytics` always resolve services asynchronously.
>     - Adapters must also use async resolution for service lookup instead of kernel's synchronous `getService()`.
> - **Best Practice:** Consider deprecating direct `getService()` access for any service interface defined as Promise-based, or add documentation warnings in ObjectStack Kernel and Adapter docs.
> 
> ## Priority
> - **High:** Breaks dispatch and dynamic service composition for any plugin using async registration.
> 
> ## References & Context
> - ObjectStack repo: [spec](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/spec)
> - Multiple test examples show async mocks (passing) but production sync lookups fail.
>
